findings.title: UC-5 iOS broadcast can never seal: the native device block lacks screenW/screenH/densityDpi/orientation the validator requires, and every UC-5 test hand-authors an Android-shaped device so the defect is invisible
findings.userImpact: Every real iOS system-broadcast (ReplayKit) session is refused at /continuous-complete with 422 CONTINUOUS_MANIFEST_INVALID ('invalid device.screenW'); the user records, uploads all segments, and then cannot obtain an Evidence record. The reserved record is released/discarded.
findings.legalImpact: UC-5 is presented as code complete with a green API suite ('accepts the DEVICE THE BROADCAST EXTENSION ACTUALLY REPORTS'); that proof statement is false — the device it sends is not the one the extension reports.
findings.reproduction: iOS: stopContinuousCapture() -> Swift ProovraBroadcastResult.toJsMap() returns device {platform:'ios', osVersion, model, appVersion} only (ProovraBroadcastShared.swift:58-63). JS buildContinuousManifest copies it verbatim (continuous-capture.ts:121). Server continuous-complete calls validateScreenContinuousManifest (continuous-capture.service.ts:94), whose loop at screen-continuous-manifest.ts:286-288 requires isNonNegInt(device.screenW/screenH/densityDpi) and :289 requires device.orientation in {portrait,landscape} -> {ok:false,'invalid device.screenW'}. Runtime probe: in uc5-ios-screen-capture.integration.test.ts replace the device literal at :253-262 with {platform:'ios',osVersion:'18.0',model:'iPhone',appVersion:'1.0.0'} (the exact Swift shape) and the seal test at :322 returns 422 instead of 200.
findings.observed: API test (uc5:253-262) supplies screenW/screenH/densityDpi/orientation that iOS never emits; shared test (screen-continuous-manifest.test.mjs:83) spreads the Android device and flips only platform; mobile e2e (capture-lifecycle-e2e.test.mjs:270-277) seals '{"segments":2}' through an always-200 transport; buildContinuousManifest is documented 'Unit-tested' (continuous-capture.ts:109) but no test imports it. The TS type ScreenContinuousDevice (index.ts:207) claims the fields exist, so tsc cannot catch it either. native-module-contract.test.mjs checks method names only.
findings.expected: At least one test builds the UC-5 manifest from the exact object the Swift module resolves (or a recorded fixture of it) through the real buildContinuousManifest and the real validator; and the Swift result supplies (or the validator tolerates, per platform) the screen geometry fields.
findings.rootCause: Test fixtures were authored from the validator/type contract instead of from the producer (Swift) output; no cross-language shape contract exists, only a name-set contract.
findings.remediation: Either emit screenW/screenH (UIScreen.main.nativeBounds), densityDpi (scale-derived) and orientation from ProovraBroadcastResult.toJsMap(), or make the validator's geometry fields platform-conditional; fix ScreenContinuousDevice typing to match. Replace hand-authored iOS device fixtures in the three suites with a single shared fixture generated from/asserted against the Swift toJsMap keys.
findings.requiredTests: 1) mobile: buildContinuousManifest(iosNativeResultFixture) passes validateScreenContinuousManifest(…,{expectedPlatform:'ios'}); 2) a source-contract guard that the key set emitted by ProovraBroadcastResult.toJsMap device == the validator's required device keys; 3) uc5 API suite uses the same fixture.
findings.runtimeProbe: Disposable-DB API test: stage a DIRECT_SCREEN_CAPTURE_IOS session exactly as uc5 stageContinuous does but with device={platform:'ios',osVersion:'18.0',model:'iPhone',appVersion:'1.0.0'}; expect 200 today it returns 422 CONTINUOUS_MANIFEST_INVALID.

findings.title: UC-1 'Chrome + Edge' browser acceptance runs the same bundled Chromium under both projects and is not wired into any CI workflow
findings.userImpact: An Edge-specific (or Chrome-Stable-specific) extension failure would be reported as 'edge PASS' by the acceptance harness; UC-1 closure is defined as 'both browser projects pass'.
findings.legalImpact: A release decision (store submission to Edge Add-ons) could rest on an acceptance verdict for a browser that was never launched.
findings.reproduction: The projects set use.channel ('chrome' / 'msedge'), but the spec never uses the browser/context fixtures: it calls chromium.launchPersistentContext(userDataDir,{headless:false,args:[--load-extension…]}) with no channel/executablePath (direct-web-capture.spec.ts:400-403). Test-level `use` options are not applied to a manually launched browser, so --project=edge launches Playwright's bundled Chromium; uc1-acceptance-windows.mjs:533-539 records results[project]='PASS' per project.
findings.observed: Both 'chromium' and 'edge' runs execute the identical binary; neither is Chrome Stable nor Edge. No workflow in .github/workflows references apps/extension/e2e, so it never runs in CI. The spec also bypasses the extension's own OAuth code (token injected into chrome.storage.session at :409-418) and asserts Library/Detail/Case/Search/Report/Package via API calls, not the UI; 'PACKAGE_VALIDATOR' reads public-verify server fields, not the offline validator.
findings.expected: Each project launches its declared channel (launchPersistentContext(dir,{channel: testInfo.project.use.channel, …})) and the harness refuses to report a project whose launched browser version string does not match the expected product.
findings.rootCause: Manual launch ignores project configuration; no assertion on the launched browser identity.
findings.remediation: Pass channel from testInfo.project.use into launchPersistentContext and assert browser.version()/userAgent contains 'Edg/' for the edge project; record the browser version in the acceptance result. Note Chrome Stable ≥137 ignores --load-extension, so the chrome project may need Chrome for Testing — decide explicitly rather than silently using bundled Chromium.
findings.requiredTests: Acceptance run prints and asserts navigator.userAgent per project.

findings.title: UC-4 worker screen-intelligence path has no CI-executed behavioural proof: the job handler is untested, the DB persistence suite is env-skipped in CI, and real OCR is never executed
findings.userImpact: A regression in the reconstruct_screen job (claim/lease/fence, storage wiring, real ffmpeg/tesseract invocation, persistence) ships green; derived keyframes/OCR/reconstruction could silently stop being produced.
findings.legalImpact: Derived-intelligence provenance (§61 link from reconstructed block back to ORIGINAL part digest) is only proven on a developer workstation, not by a gate.
findings.reproduction: grep -rn processReconstructScreenJob services/*/test e2e -> no hits. uc4-screen-intelligence-persistence.integration.test.ts:33-34 is `describe.skip` unless TEST_DATABASE_URL; the worker has no integration project and ci.yml 'Test — worker' (:391-394) sets no TEST_DATABASE_URL (only schema-reproducibility.yml:241 does, for the API project). That suite also injects fakeOcr and fakeKeyframeProducer (:62-105). uc4-tesseract-ocr.test.ts:55-61: when tesseract is present the only assertion is typeof provider.version === 'string'; when absent it asserts fail-closed — real extraction is asserted in neither branch. uc4-keyframe-producer.test.ts:48,74 ctx.skip() when ffmpeg is unavailable (docs/operations/external-proof-register.md:42 says CI availability is unverified).
findings.observed: Worker-side UC-4 is covered only by pure-core unit tests plus uc4-guards.test.ts SOURCE_STRING regexes over the handler/service source.
findings.expected: A CI-executed test drives processReconstructScreenJob (or the processor dispatch for kind 'reconstruct_screen') against a disposable DB + in-memory store, and at least one assertion on real tesseract text output where the runtime is installed.
findings.rootCause: Worker integration suites were written against the API's TEST_DATABASE_URL convention but the worker has no CI step that provides a database.
findings.remediation: Add a worker integration step to schema-reproducibility.yml (same Postgres + P7_TEST_REDIS_URL) running the worker *.integration.test.ts, or move these suites into the API integration project; add a handler-level test; assert recognised text in the tesseract present-branch and fail (not skip) in CI when ffmpeg-static did not install.
findings.requiredTests: processReconstructScreenJob happy path + lease-lost fence + OCR-disabled PARTIAL against live PG16 in CI.

findings.title: Object-Lock package/report publication suite never runs in CI although ci.yml starts a MinIO and states it is for that suite
findings.userImpact: The streamed-package staging → checksum → promote → VersionId pin path (the one that failed in production, Sentry 150024171) has no gate; a regression publishes nothing or publishes unlocked.
findings.legalImpact: Package immutability claims (COMPLIANCE retention applied, VersionId pinned) are asserted by a suite that no gate executes.
findings.reproduction: The suite is `describe.skip` unless OBJECT_LOCK_MINIO_ENDPOINT is set (:33-34). No workflow, bootstrap or setup file sets OBJECT_LOCK_MINIO_ENDPOINT (repo-wide grep hits only the test file). The CI MinIO step (ci.yml:367-389) listens on :59000 and creates `point7-local-bucket` WITHOUT --with-lock, while the suite requires an object-locked bucket with default COMPLIANCE retention (test header :9-16). The comment at ci.yml:335-352 says the step exists because this file had five failures — stale since the file was converted to the env-gated form.
findings.observed: Suite reports as skipped in CI; the CI comment and MinIO container create the impression it runs. docs/operations/external-proof-register.md:41 correctly says 'nowhere yet'.
findings.expected: Either CI creates a locked bucket and exports OBJECT_LOCK_MINIO_* so the suite runs, or the ci.yml step/comment is removed so nothing implies coverage.
findings.rootCause: Harness replaced (c8291b86 → 76fddb72) without updating the CI step that served the old harness.
findings.remediation: In ci.yml create `mc mb --with-lock` + `mc retention set --default COMPLIANCE 1d` and export OBJECT_LOCK_MINIO_ENDPOINT/_LOGIN/_PASSPHRASE/_BUCKET for the worker step; make a skipped run of this file a CI failure.
findings.requiredTests: The existing 4 cases executed in CI.

findings.title: Capture refusal/fail-closed assertions accept any non-200 (a 500 crash passes), and the UC-5 'unknown platform refused' case cannot isolate the platform check
findings.userImpact: A refusal path that regresses into an unhandled 500 (user sees 'problem on our side', record possibly left reserved) still passes.
findings.reproduction: uc5:338 mutates device.platform in an already-declared manifest, so the bytes no longer match the declared manifest digest; the refusal at :344 (`not.toBe(200)`) is satisfied by the artifact-mismatch gate (or a 500) even if the platform allow-list were deleted — the test's own comment concedes 'refused on both counts'. uc3:455 / uc5:371 and uc0:692/697/893 (`toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(400)`) likewise pass on 5xx.
findings.observed: Weak status assertions on the negative paths.
findings.expected: Assert the exact status + denial code (e.g. 422 CONTINUOUS_MANIFEST_INVALID with error mentioning device.platform, declared before upload so the digest matches).
findings.rootCause: Deliberately loose assertions ('rather than a brittle exact code').
findings.remediation: Pin status and denial; for the platform case, upload the forged manifest as the declared part so only the platform gate can refuse it.

findings.title: Capture commercial-gate 'allowed' cases pass on any thrown error except TEAM_PLAN_REQUIRED (including DB-unavailable)
findings.userImpact: A regression that refuses capture in a correctly-planned workspace with another code (or crashes) is not caught by this suite.
findings.reproduction: Both blocks do `if (caught) { expect(caught.code).not.toBe('TEAM_PLAN_REQUIRED') }`; the unit project has no database, so assertWorkspaceAllowsEvidenceCreation for SHARED/TEAM throws an infra error that the test explicitly tolerates (comment at :203-208). The positive path is therefore never asserted in the unit run.
findings.observed: ALWAYS_TRUE for the positive half of the matrix (templates × SHARED/TEAM and SINGLE_OCCUPANT/FREE).
findings.expected: Positive path asserted to resolve, in an integration test with a DB (the UC suites do set ENTERPRISE/ACTIVE and seal successfully, which partially covers it).
findings.rootCause: Unit test for a DB-backed gate.
findings.remediation: Move the matrix to an integration suite or inject the count query.
